articles.title: Nokia and SoftBank Corp. agree to conduct commercial AI-RAN field trial in Japan

ai_insights.summary: Nokia and SoftBank have announced a 2027 commercial field trial in Japan to validate AI-RAN technology. Utilizing NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform and Nokia’s anyRAN software, the trial aims to orchestrate AI and RAN workloads on a single platform, serving as a critical evolution path toward AI-native 6G architectures.
key_evidence: Nokia and SoftBank to conduct commercial AI-RAN field trial in Japan in 2027.
The deployment uses Nokia’s anyRAN software on SoftBank’s AITRAS platform with NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC).
The trial provides an evolution path toward AI-native 6G by running RAN workloads on cloud-native infrastructure alongside AI workloads.
Hardware includes NVIDIA Grace CPU, NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 GPU, and NVIDIA ConnectX-8 networking.
Integration of Nokia MantaRay and AITRAS Orchestrator for coordinated AI and RAN resource management.

articles.summary: Espoo, Finland – Nokia today announced an agreement with SoftBank Corp. to conduct a commercial AI-RAN field trial in Japan in 2027. The planned deployment will use Nokia’s anyRAN software on SoftBank’s AITRAS, its core platform for AI-RAN, with NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC), in conjunction with the AITRAS Orchestrator. The companies plan to validate AI-RAN technology in a commercial network environment under commercial traffic conditions. The upcoming field trial will assess key AI-RAN capabilities in a live commercial network environment and represents an important step in SoftBank’s efforts to commercialize AI-RAN. It will also advance Nokia’s AI-RAN commercialization roadmap by moving the technology from laboratory development toward real-world deployment. The planned trial will combine Nokia’s AI-native anyRAN Cloud RAN software on a SoftBank AITRAS platform with NVIDIA’s ARC platform and the AITRAS Orchestrator. The accelerated computing platform incorporates an NVIDIA Grace CPU, NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 GPU and NVIDIA ConnectX-8 networking, providing the computing and high-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity needed to run commercial RAN workloads on cloud-native infrastructure. The AITRAS Orchestrator will support the orchestration of AI and RAN workloads within the trial environment, while NVIDIA’s programmable accelerated computing platform and NVIDIA CUDA ecosystem provide a software-defined foundation for continued AI-RAN innovation and an evolution path toward AI-native 6G. The trial will also demonstrate how Nokia's AI-native anyRAN software can operate within the SoftBank AITRAS platform architecture, highlighting deployment flexibility beyond traditional RAN implementations. As demand for generative, agentic and physical AI applications continues to grow, operators require networks that can efficiently support increasing data volumes while enabling new AI-driven services closer to the end user. By combining Nokia’s AI-native RAN software with NVIDIA accelerated computing, AI-RAN brings radio and AI workloads onto a common platform, helping operators improve infrastructure utilization, accelerate innovation and unlock new revenue opportunities. The agreement builds on Nokia and SoftBank’s ongoing collaboration in AI-RAN, supported by NVIDIA’s accelerated computing node. The planned field trial will bring together Nokia’s AI-native RAN software with SoftBank’s AITRAS platform including the AITRAS Orchestrator to test AI-RAN under commercial traffic conditions. The collaboration will explore how AI and RAN workloads can be orchestrated on a common platform while preserving carrier-grade RAN operational requirements. Integration between Nokia MantaRay and the AITRAS Orchestrator will help enable coordinated management of AI and RAN resources, creating a foundation for future AI-native network architectures. The trial will contribute to the broader industry transition toward AI-native network architectures and explore how operators can introduce new capabilities faster while supporting emerging AI applications at the network edge. The planned trial will also explore AI-RAN’s potential to support richer AI-driven experiences, lower-latency services and new applications powered by real-time intelligence. Future use cases could include physical AI, immersive digital experiences, robotics and autonomous systems that require close interaction between AI and connectivity.

articles.summary: Nokia Corporation Interim report 22 October 2026 at 08:00 EEST Nokia Corporation Interim Report for Q3 2026 Nokia delivers strong net sales and profit growth Q3 net sales grew 9% y-o-y on a constant currency basis (+10% reported). Network Infrastructure net sales grew 15% y-o-y on a constant currency basis, led by IP Networks growing 43% and Optical Networks 18%. Group net sales to AI & Cloud customers grew 123% and order intake 118%. Mobile Infrastructure net sales grew 5% y-o-y, in part due to acceleration of revenue from Q4 into Q3. The segment benefited from product mix, commercial discipline and continued execution of the cost reduction program. Q3 comparable gross margin was largely stable y-o-y at 44.6%. Reported gross margin declined 220bps to 42.2%. Q3 comparable operating margin increased 220bps y-o-y to 11.7% benefiting from revenue growth and operating efficiency. Reported operating margin declined 160bps to 3.8% due to accelerated restructuring and integration cost. Q3 comparable diluted EPS from continued operations of EUR 0.09; reported diluted EPS from continued operations of EUR 0.03. Nokia's full year financial outlook is unchanged. "Team Nokia continues to deliver on our commitments as we execute against our strategy. In Q3, we grew net sales by 9% and improved comparable operating margin by 220 basis points. We continue to simplify our portfolio, and we are on track to complete the Infinera integration by the end of 2026, one year ahead of plan with EUR 200 million of net synergies. In AI & Cloud, net sales more than doubled year-over-year and we secured EUR 1.5 billion in new orders. Our strong order backlog also positions us for future growth. We expect our combined Optical and IP Networks businesses to grow between 25% and 30% in 2027. Nokia’s strengths are uniquely suited to meet growing demands for AI infrastructure that is larger, more distributed and hyperconnected. We are investing where we can differentiate and co-innovate with hyperscalers. Our partnership with Google in support of their EUR 13 billion investment in Finland is an example of how our optical and IP networks provide the critical connectivity AI infrastructure requires. AI-native networks are moving into the physical world, and our AI-RAN platform is being developed to deliver the performance needed for this market. Together with T-Mobile and NVIDIA, we completed the world’s first AI-RAN call in a live operator network in line with the commitment we announced last year. As we move towards commercial deployment the features and spectral efficiency delivered by our platform are uniquely differentiated in the market. Overall, growth is accelerating, operating leverage is becoming more visible and I’m confident in the long-term shareholder value Team Nokia is creating." executive_briefing:
Strategic Overview

The strategic landscape for 6G is currently defined by the convergence of "physical AI" and the transition of non-terrestrial networks from experimental labs to commercial reality. A primary theme is the emergence of AI-RAN, exemplified by the Nokia-SoftBank-NVIDIA partnership, which seeks to integrate agentic AI platforms for autonomous network management. Simultaneously, the industry is shifting its focus toward Key Value Indicators such as sustainability and "network of networks" architectures. This move is complemented by the rapid commercialization of direct-to-device satellite services, which are now being deployed for service continuity in regions ranging from Ukraine to Western Europe, signaling a broader push for ubiquitous connectivity.

Standardization Velocity

Standardization efforts within the 3GPP are accelerating as the industry narrows its technical focus for the upcoming 6G era. Release 21 currently shows a standardization velocity of 33.3% completion across 45 identified work and study items. This pacing reflects a disciplined transition from high-level research into the rigorous specification phase required for global interoperability. Despite prevailing capital expenditure concerns and "money problems" within the telco sector, this 33.3% progress rate suggests that the technical foundations for AI-integrated radio and satellite-land convergence are being formalized according to schedule, setting the stage for the first wave of 6G-ready commercial deployments.

Geopolitical Signals

Geopolitically, regional signals indicate a sharpening competition over technological sovereignty and market leadership. The European Union is aggressively funding the translation of 6G research into industrial innovation through the SNS JU, with a specific focus on sovereign AI and secure API enforcement to maintain digital autonomy. In the East, Japan has positioned itself as a critical proving ground for AI-RAN field trials, leveraging strategic partnerships with European vendors to lead in hardware-AI convergence. Meanwhile, the North American market is characterized by aggressive leadership claims from carriers like T-Mobile, who aim for early 6G dominance while navigating the complexities of satellite land-grabs and tower infrastructure premiums.
